body.statement:
For a multiplier in a fixed compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), Kennedy's sample-split estimator averages held-out fitted uncentered influence-function values and estimates variance by their empirical second moment centered at the estimator.  Denote the resulting estimator and standard-error scale at a fixed multiplier \(\delta_0\) by \(\widehat\psi^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)\) and \(\widehat\sigma^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)\), respectively.  Under the conditions of his weak-convergence theorem, the pointwise ninety-five percent interval is
\[
\left[
\widehat\psi^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)-1.96\frac{\widehat\sigma^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)}{\sqrt n},\;
\widehat\psi^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)+1.96\frac{\widehat\sigma^{\mathrm K}(\delta_0)}{\sqrt n}
\right].
\]

source.locator: Section 4.2, sample-splitting estimator; Theorem 3 and the immediately following pointwise-confidence-interval paragraph
source.verbatim_statement: For each δ and fold k, the sample-splitting algorithm computes fitted held-out influence-function values and defines ψ̂_k(δ) to be their average in the test data; ψ̂(δ) is the average of the K fold estimators. Theorem 3 defines σ̂²(δ)=P_n[{φ(Z;η̂_{−S},δ)−ψ̂(δ)}²]. Based on Theorem 3, pointwise 95% confidence intervals are ψ̂(δ) ± 1.96 σ̂(δ)/√n.

attestation.note: Verified directly against Algorithm 1 in Section 4.2, Theorem 3, and the immediately following pointwise interval paragraph in arXiv:1704.00211v3, pp. 11–13.
